detail: Claim: when a close hook signals (fnn-pull-service-close re-signals a retained cleanup debt), the stop function at owner.lisp:8865-8868 catches it as (serious-condition () (setq modules-joined nil)); fnn-err names it at :8873/:8902 ('a close hook failed'); the final join block (:8903-8920, fnn-owner-feed-close-all, log settlement, journal close) runs only when modules-joined is true; so the log-close-action is not :joined and the exit is not clean. That is the fence for the debt: the condition is reduced to a flag, and the flag withholds clean close. Unverified: that modules-joined=nil forces a non-clean exit code (the path from log-close-action not :joined to the process exit code, owner.lisp after :8935), and that no other exit path ignores it. Would verify: a checker row naming the flag, requiring every dolist-funcall handler clause to clear it, that the clean-close block is guarded by it as a conjunct of the when test, and that the else path reaches a fence function or a non-zero exit (fence_functions). Or an ACL2/host test with a failing hook asserting exit code 3. Sequences after rl02 (owner.lisp claimed).

title: Stop path: a failed close hook clears modules-joined; is that the fence?
